summary: Byzanz is a fast, tight bidding game where the same cards in your hand are both your currency and your potential winnings, forcing constant trade-offs between bidding aggressively now and hoarding value for later. It's a short, sharp filler that rewards reading the market and opponents' hands more than deep strategy.
praised: clever dual-use-card mechanism (cards are both money and points)
criticised: can feel swingy or luck-dependent with the auction order
less impactful with lower player counts

interaction.detail: Players bid against each other for shared market offers using cards from their own hand, so every bid affects what remains available and how much competitors can spend later. There's no shared board beyond the market itself; most of the game state is what's visible in each player's hand and completed sets.

win_criteria: Most points, one or two sources

scoring.why: The winner is whoever accumulates the most valuable completed sets of goods cards by game end.
scoring.how_you_win: You win by successfully bidding on and collecting sets of three matching goods cards, using your remaining hand cards as bidding currency until the deck runs out.
